question: Will any of OpenAI’s “Ten Advances in Math and Theoretical CS” be shown to be flawed by the end of August?
resolution_criteria:
[tweet]YES if, by August 31, there is a consensus in credible reporting or within the academic community that at least one of the core arguments or main theorems in OpenAI's "Ten Advances" is fatally flawed or incorrect. Otherwise, resolves NO.

"Flawed" means a core mathematical or theoretical error is identified that invalidates the main result of the paper, and the error is either unfixable or difficult to patch.

Nitpicks—such as minor typos, formatting errors, minor translation gaps in the Lean formalization that do not undermine the mathematical proof's validity, or easily patchable edge cases—do not count toward a YES resolution.
research:
I found no evidence, as of 2026-08-16, that any of the ten results has been shown fatally flawed. The one error claim I found says a lemma's printed proof is wrong but the lemma's statement still holds, and it offers its own repair. The other main criticism is about missing credit for prior work, not correctness. My page fetches were all refused by the proxy, so everything below comes from search-result summaries rather than pages I read myself. I left out material dated after 2026-08-16.

## 1. Resolution source
- There is no single data source. The question resolves on whether credible reporting or the academic community agrees that a core result is fatally flawed.
- 2026-08-01: OpenAI published "Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science," a 249-page manuscript (one source says the PDF went up July 31). It credits an internal model ("Astra") and comes with Lean 4 certificates in the openai/ten-proofs GitHub repository. [the-decoder](https://the-decoder.com/openai-announces-its-next-major-model-astra-by-dropping-ten-previously-unsolved-math-solutions/), [qz](https://qz.com/openai-astra-model-math-problems-lean-proofs-080326), [forklog](https://forklog.com/en/news/openai-says-internal-astra-model-produced-10-results-in-mathematics-and-theoretical-computer-science)
- One write-up says the formalization reports sorry_count 0 and uses only the standard axioms. Commentators point out this doesn't show the Lean statements match the original open problems, and that community review of that question was still pending. [packetnebula](https://packetnebula.com/articles/openai-astra-ten-lean-proofs/), [mlq.ai](https://mlq.ai/news/openai-publishes-ten-claimed-math-advances-with-formal-peer-review-still-pending/), [s5labs](https://s5labs.io/resources/insights/openai-astra-ten-math-proofs-lean-certificates/)
- None of the results had been through formal journal refereeing. [kingy.ai](https://kingy.ai/news/openai-astra-ten-math-results-evidence/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question. I found no consensus, and no strong individual claim, that a main theorem is fatally wrong.
- 2026-08-03: Mikołaj and Krzysztof Sienicki posted an 8-page arXiv note. It says the printed proof of a greedy conditioning lemma in Chapter 6 reverses a condition, and it gives a counterexample to the printed procedure. The authors say the lemma itself is true and offer a corrected proof they call a "local repair." That looks like a patchable issue, not a fatal one. I couldn't open the note itself. [aiunderstanding.org](https://aiunderstanding.org/news/audit-of-an-openai-ai-generated-proof-finds-a-reversed-condition-and-publishes-a-r)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- About 2026-08-13: Huxiu reports that OpenAI dropped the "at least a decade" wording from its announcement without publishing a list of corrections. [huxiu](https://m.huxiu.com/article/4882806.html)
- 2026-08-12: Commentary pieces about AI and mathematics; none reports a proof error. [mappingignorance](https://mappingignorance.org/2026/08/12/generative-ai-has-changed-mathematics-forever/)
- About 2026-08-06: Scientific American quoted experts calling the release "research misconduct":
  - Steven Miller (Yeshiva University) says the sphere-packing proof reuses his 2016 argument without credit.
  - Francesco Fournier-Facio (Cambridge) says the non-sofic groups result combines ideas from 2016 and 2019 papers.
  - OpenAI says it stands by the results being correct and plans a minor update to fix the citations.
  - These are credit disputes, not claimed errors. [SciAm](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/openais-latest-math-breakthroughs-commit-research-misconduct-experts-say/), [aiweekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/openais-astra-math-proofs-draw-research-misconduct-claims), [cryptobriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/openai-backlash-math-discovery-astra/)
- 2026-08-03: Max Weinreich's essay "The crisis of AI-generated mathematics" argues against AI in mathematics. It mentions OpenAI's ten solutions but, judging from the abstract, claims no specific error. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.02859), [alphaxiv](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2608.02859)
- 2026-08-03: The Sienicki Chapter 6 lemma note described in section 2.
- Gary Marcus called the model "amazing but vastly oversold." I didn't see a claimed proof error in the summary. [Substack](https://garymarcus.substack.com/p/openais-amazing-but-vastly-oversold)

## 4. Base rates
- I couldn't find a systematic base rate.
- For comparison, earlier high-profile AI math claims (for example the 2025 Erdős-problem episodes) mostly fell apart over prior literature or overclaiming, not over invalid proofs. The early pattern here is the same: credit disputes rather than errors.
- Lean-verified results seldom turn out wrong in the formal sense. The usual way they fail is that the formal statement doesn't match the intended problem, and spotting that tends to take weeks of expert checking.
- The window left is only about 15 days, and the question requires consensus, which usually takes longer than that to form.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Manifold, "Will any of OpenAI's 'Ten Advances…' be shown to be flawed by the end of August?":
  - 2026-08-03 snapshot: about 8%, with 22 traders.
  - Another snapshot shows about 39%, but I couldn't confirm its date or whether it was before 2026-08-16.
  - Commenters there doubted one cited philosophy-paper critique.
  - I couldn't load the page for the current price. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Sketchy/will-any-of-openais-ten-advances-in)
- I found no Polymarket or Kalshi market on this.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- OpenAI's promised "minor update" for citations could come out. That would address credit, not correctness.
- The authors or others could respond to the Sienicki Chapter 6 claim. If it's confirmed, it would probably count as patchable, since the authors themselves offer a repair.
- Experts in each field are still checking whether each Lean statement matches the original problem. A mismatch found there is the most plausible route to a "core flaw" claim.
- A further arXiv audit, "A Human Audit of OpenAI's AI-Generated Mathematical Proofs" (arXiv 2608.14673), exists. I couldn't confirm when it was first posted or what it said as of 2026-08-16. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.14673)
